Definition: from ἁνδάνω (to please); sensual delight; by implication, desire:--lust, pleasure.
BiblicalUsage: Hedone is pleasure, lust, the craving for what feels good, and James names it as the root of war. In James 4:1 wars come from the lusts that war in the members, in James 4:3 men ask and do not receive because they ask to spend it on their lusts, in Luke 8:14 the seed is choked by the pleasures of this life, and in Titus 3:3 Paul says we were once serving divers lusts and pleasures.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe James is right about where fights start: not in the other person, but in the pleasure I want and cannot have. The seed that falls among pleasures does not die loudly, it is simply choked, and that quiet death is the one I should fear most.
